title: Immunomagnetic Enrichment of CD8 T Cells from Murine Tissues
author: Trolio, Duong, et al.
materials: MACS buffer (PBS, pH 7.2 with 0.5% BSA and 2 mM EDTA)
DMEM (high glucose + glutamine + pyruvate) with 10% HI-NCS

steps.title: Prepare liver single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Generate a leukocyte single‑cell suspension from mouse liver using mechanical dissociation, Percoll density centrifugation, RBC lysis, and filtration.

substeps.instruction: Place the liver in a 70 µm cell strainer atop a 50 mL tube.
Gently mash the liver through the strainer with the plunger of a 3 mL syringe, rinsing with FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C; discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 42 % Percoll and transfer to a 15 mL tube.
Rinse the original tube with an additional 4 mL of 42 % Percoll and add to the 15 mL tube (Percoll must be at 21–23 °C).
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 20 min at 21–23 °C with the brake OFF.
Remove and discard the top cellular layer and Percoll, leaving the leukocyte pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL RBC Lysis buffer and transfer to a new 15 mL tube containing 4.9 mL RBC Lysis buffer.
Use 100 µL of this suspension to wash the bottom of the original tube; add the wash to the rest of the cell suspension and mix well.
Incubate for 5 min at 21–23 °C.
Add 5 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min (pellet should appear pale).
Rinse a 20 µm pre‑separation filter with 500 µL FACS buffer and place it atop a fresh 15 mL tube.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer and pass through the filter, rinsing the filter with additional FACS buffer.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 300 × g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 100 µL MACS buffer and set aside 5 µL for cell counting.

steps.title: Prepare heart single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Obtain a leukocyte suspension from mouse heart by gentleMACS mechanical dissociation, Percoll gradient, RBC lysis, and filtration.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the heart to a 60 mm petri dish and cover with chilled DMEM + 10 % heat‑inactivated newborn calf serum (HI‑NCS).
Cut the heart into quarters with a scalpel and place the pieces into a C tube containing 5 mL DMEM + 10 % HI‑NCS.
Close the C tube tightly, attach it upside‑down to the sleeve of the gentleMACS Dissociator, and run program m_impTumor_02 followed by m_impTumor_03.
Optional: briefly centrifuge the C tube to collect tissue at the bottom.
Place a 70 µm cell strainer atop a 50 mL tube.
Mash the heart tissue through the strainer with the plunger of a 3 mL syringe, rinsing with DMEM + 10 % HI‑NCS.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C; discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 42 % Percoll and transfer to a 15 mL tube.
Rinse the original tube with 4 mL of 42 % Percoll and add to the 15 mL tube (Percoll at 21–23 °C).
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 20 min at 21–23 °C with the brake OFF.
Discard the top cellular layer and Percoll.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL RBC Lysis buffer and transfer to a new 15 mL tube containing 900 µL RBC Lysis buffer.
Use 100 µL of this suspension to wash the bottom of the original tube; add the wash to the rest of the suspension and mix.
Incubate for 2 min at 21–23 °C.
Add 5 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min (pellet should be pale).
Rinse a 20 µm pre‑separation filter with 500 µL FACS buffer and place it atop a fresh 15 mL tube.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer, pass through the filter, and rinse the filter with additional FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 100 µL MACS buffer and set aside 5 µL for counting.

steps.title: Prepare kidney single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Isolate leukocytes from mouse kidney using dounce homogenization, a two‑step Percoll gradient, and filtration.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the kidney to a 60 mm petri dish and cover with DMEM + 10 % HI‑NCS.
Cut the kidney into ~3 mm pieces with a scalpel.
Place the pieces into a pre‑chilled dounce homogenizer containing ~5 mL chilled DMEM + 10 % HI‑NCS.
Homogenize on ice by twisting the pestle and repeatedly inserting the long end, keeping the pestle below the liquid surface to avoid bubbles.
Place a 70 µm cell strainer atop a 50 mL tube.
Mash the homogenate through the strainer with the plunger of a 3 mL syringe, rinsing with FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C; discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of 44 % Percoll.
Transfer 3 mL of 70 % Percoll into a clean 15 mL tube (Percoll at 21–23 °C).
Slowly overlay the 44 % Percoll suspension onto the 70 % Percoll layer.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 20 min at 21–23 °C with acceleration set to 6 and the brake OFF.
Discard the top cellular layer.
Collect the interphase (leukocytes) and transfer to a new 15 mL tube.
Bring the volume to 15 mL with FACS buffer, invert to mix, and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min to pellet the cells.
Rinse a 20 µm pre‑separation filter with 500 µL FACS buffer and place it atop a fresh 15 mL tube.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer, pass through the filter, and rinse with additional FACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in 100 µL MACS buffer and set aside 5 µL for counting.

steps.title: Prepare bone marrow single‑cell suspension
steps.instruction: Generate a leukocyte suspension from mouse bone marrow by mechanical crushing, Percoll gradient, and filtration (no RBC lysis).

substeps.instruction: Place a 70 µm cell strainer atop a 50 mL tube.
Put the bones into a mortar and add ~1 mL FACS buffer per bone.
Crush each bone firmly with a pestle until the bone appears clear and marrow is released.
Pass the released liquid through the 70 µm strainer.
Mash the marrow on the strainer with the plunger of a 3 mL syringe, rinsing with FACS buffer.
Rinse the bones, mortar, and pestle with FACS buffer and pass this rinse through the same strainer.
Centrifuge the collected suspension at 300 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C; discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of 44 % Percoll.
Transfer 3 mL of 70 % Percoll into a clean 15 mL tube (Percoll at 21–23 °C).
Slowly overlay the 44 % Percoll suspension onto the 70 % Percoll layer.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 20 min at 21–23 °C with acceleration 6 and the brake OFF.
Discard the top cellular layer.
Collect the interphase (leukocytes) and transfer to a new 15 mL tube.
Bring the volume to 15 mL with FACS buffer, invert to mix, and centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min to pellet the cells.
Rinse a 20 µm pre‑separation filter with 500 µL FACS buffer and place it atop a fresh 15 mL tube.
Resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer, pass through the filter, and rinse; if the filter becomes blocked, scrape the bottom with a transfer pipette (do NOT replace the filter with a larger one).
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the final pellet in ~6 mL MACS buffer and set aside 5 µL for counting (do NOT perform RBC lysis on bone marrow).

steps.title: Stain cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Label enriched cells with viability dye and surface antibodies, fix, and prepare for acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 0.1–4 × 10^6 cells per well of a 96‑well U‑bottom plate.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C; discard the supernatant.
Wash: resuspend cells in 150 µL PBS, centrifuge 200 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 40 µL Zombie UV diluted 1:1000 in PBS.
Incubate in the dark for 20 min at 21–23 °C.
Add 150 µL FACS buffer, pellet at 200 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C, and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 40 µL surface‑antibody cocktail (as defined in Table 2).
Incubate in the dark for 20 min at 21–23 °C.
Add 150 µL FACS buffer, pellet at 200 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C, and discard supernatant.
Wash cells with 150 µL FACS buffer (resuspend and centrifuge as above).
Resuspend cells in 100 µL 1× BD Stabilizing Fixative.
Incubate in the dark for 15 min at 21–23 °C.
Add 100 µL FACS buffer, pellet at 200 × g for 3 min at 21–23 °C, and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100 µL FACS buffer.
Transfer the samples to appropriate tubes or plates for flow‑cytometer acquisition.
Pause point: samples may be stored up to 4 days at 4 °C protected from light before analysis.

description: The following protocol describes the isolation and enrichment of mouse CD8 T cells by immunomagnetic positive selection. This protocol is specific to the enrichment of CD8 T cells. Substitution with other commercial kits to enrich alternative leukocyte subsets would require validation. Tissue processing steps have been individually optimized for each organ to maximize tissue-specific enrichment efficiency. For CD8 T cell enrichment from spleen and lymph node tissue, adherence to the manufacturer’s standard instructions is generally sufficient. The time specified for the enrichment step is for a single sample. Several samples can be enriched at once using multiple magnets, though staggered incubation times are recommended. Preparation of required reagents and materials in advance is essential to minimize cell death and maximize yield.
